nom: Dr Dennis Gross Alpha Beta Universal Daily Peel: for Uneven Tone or Texture and Fine Lines or Enlarged Pores

segments.dry: One reviewer with dry skin reports it works well to remove dark spots with weekly use.
segments.combination: One reviewer with sensitive-to-combination skin reports a brighter, more even glow with no irritation.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin generally report no irritation when starting slowly (every other day rather than daily), describing refreshed, non-irritated skin.
segments.normal: One reviewer with normal skin and some hyperpigmentation found it did little for her hyperpigmentation and felt too expensive for the limited results.
segments.mature: One middle-aged reviewer reports a dramatic reduction in long-standing facial redness, smaller-looking pores and faded sunspots after her very first use; another in her 40s reports a brighter, natural glow with no irritation.

concerns.aging: Reports conflict sharply: several reviewers say the peel did nothing for their fine lines or wrinkles after five to ten days of use, with one saying her wrinkles looked worse afterward, while other reviewers report smaller-looking pores and smoother texture without commenting on wrinkles specifically improving.
concerns.redness: Material is limited to one dramatic case: a reviewer with 15 years of persistent facial redness reports it was visibly gone the morning after her very first use.
concerns.spots: Reports conflict: several reviewers say they saw no change in sunspots, dark spots or hyperpigmentation after five to ten days of use, while others report sunspots and dark spots visibly faded, in one case after just one use.
concerns.blemishes: Material is limited to two reviewers who report noticeably fewer blackheads and waking up with blemish-free skin after use.

extraits.titre: Not sure what the hype is about
extraits.texte: Well, I got influenced and bought this. This “peel” did nothing for me. I followed the instructions, used the treatment every other day for 10 days. See pictures. Nothing changed in regard to sunspots, fine lines, etc.

I really thought that this would improve my wrinkles and hyper pigmentation, but it didn’t. As you can see in the before photos the red ones and in the after photos, there is no visible difference after five days of consecutive use. It does make your skin soft, but I think it is made my wrinkles look worse.

This product was praised online. Not sure why. This was nothing to write home about. Not sure if what everyone goes on about but it did no more for my skin than the dollar tree dermisil toner does. Granted I don't have acne prone skin. I have normal skin beside some hyperpigmentation. Too expensive for little results (for me)

I don't think I have ever written a review for a product in my life. I realize the lighting is different in these shots, but I didn't take a 'before' shot because I wasn't expecting to share anything with anyone. Actually, I was messaging my friend and telling her how shocked I was at these results, and I sent her these two photos this morning. So, then, I figured I should share them here because a product this good deserves some praise. One photo is of me outside a few days ago (with my natural redness—not flushed—that is just what my skin has looked like for the past 15 years or so), and then there is a photo of myself this morning, outside, after using just one of these pads. It was my first pad and my first time ever doing a peel. I used this wipe/pad last night, and when I woke up this morning, I genuinely thought my bathroom light was broken. My face looked.... so.... blue and pale?! Then, I flipped the switch on and off and realized my bathroom was fine, and my face wasn't blue. I just wasn't red anymore. I was still in shock so I went to the other bathroom and stared and stared. Are my pores smaller?! Are the little tiny warmish sun spots on my face...gone?! How did it do that?! My face wasn't even peeling or dry like I assumed it would be. Instead, it was dewy and pale. I don't think it removed any wrinkles, but it made me look like a moist newborn (with the same wrinkles??) who had never stepped into the sun.
